changes.headline: Isaias post-tropical; Friday round trip closes firmer; US strikes Iran; fresh tanker hit NW of Oman
changes.dek: Isaias post-tropical; BSEE ~71.5% shut in Friday; WTI $91.85 (+$0.36), Brent $104.72 (+$0.44) Friday settles; US struck Iranian targets late Friday; UKMTO tanker hit NW of Oman ~02:00 MDT Saturday. Hurricane Isaias made landfall in the western Florida Panhandle (near Pensacola, east of Mobile) Friday night as a strong Category 2 (110 mph, 967 mb at the 8pm ET advisory) and was post-tropical by 08:01 UTC Saturday. BSEE Friday: ~71.5% of Gulf of Mexico oil shut in (~1.5 Mb/d per AP wire), 58.8% of gas; 129 of 371 platforms evacuated. Cumulative loss ~9 Mbbl (Earth Science Associates). Friday's session was a round trip: a morning selloff on Trump's Iran comments ('constructive talks,' no US strike before the Nov 3 midterms) took Brent to ~$102.60-102.80 and WTI to ~$90.18-90.43 intraday, then recovery into the close on the storm's final approach: WTI Nov26 settled $91.85 (+$0.36), Brent Dec26 $104.72 (+$0.44) (Dow Jones via Morningstar). Late Friday the US struck Iranian military targets in retaliation for Thursday's drone attacks on ships in the Strait (4 launched, 1 hit the M/V Ever Lovely). At ~02:00 MDT Saturday UKMTO reported a tanker struck by an unidentified projectile NW of Oman (bridge damaged, crew safe). Overnight tape steady: WTI ~$91.6-91.7, within ~20c of Friday's settle (indicative, thin weekend tape).
changes.balance_read: The storm's barrels come back in days; the war premium does not. Friday night's US retaliatory strikes plus the 02:00 MDT UKMTO tanker hit keep the premium two-sided into the weekend.
changes.publishers: NHC, Oct 10, 2026; BSEE via AP wire, Oct 9, 2026; Dow Jones via Morningstar, Oct 9, 2026; NYT/WSJ via wire, Oct 9-10, 2026; UKMTO via Ship and Bunker, Oct 10, 2026

changes.headline: Trump-Putin diesel deal and OFAC General License 135: the crack regime's biggest fundamental threat
changes.dek: GL-135 through Apr 7, 2027; diesel futures -4.6% Friday post-settle; crack closed $107.16 (5th day $100+ streak). Trump announced on Truth Social after a Putin call that Russia will supply 300,000+ tons of diesel 'immediately,' 500,000 tons in November, 1 million tons 'immediately thereafter,' plus 3 million tons more depending on refinery conditions. Hours later Treasury/OFAC issued General License 135 authorizing sale, delivery, and import of Russian-origin diesel through April 7, 2027 - six months, the first diesel waiver longer than 30 days since the war began. Moscow confirmed (Deputy PM Novak: 300k October / 500k November / 1M December, potentially 3 Mt/month long-term). Diesel futures fell 4.6% Friday post-settle. Caveats: Moscow has not confirmed deliverability (Ukraine is hitting Russian refineries weekly - four this week including the ~440 kb/d Omsk plant); EU/UK sanctions unchanged; volumes are announcements, not loadings. The NYMEX diesel crack closed Friday at $107.16 (validated history) - fifth day of the $100+ streak, well under Thursday night's $111.60 overnight print; all-time max $117.92 (Sep 16), not a record. 3-2-1 at $66.75 vs $75.31 max (Aug 28). Also bearish for products: China resuming refined fuel exports after Golden Week (Reuters, Oct 9); IEA prioritizing diesel in the accelerated release (Oct 7). Tightness context: AAA US diesel $6.23/gal Oct 9 (record $6.52 Sep 22); US diesel stocks at record seasonal low since 1982.
changes.balance_read: Three bearish inputs on the crack at once (Russian diesel, China fuel exports resuming, IEA diesel prioritization) against record-low US diesel stocks and $6.23/gal retail. The regime is now a two-way trade, not a long.
changes.publishers: Truth Social / OFAC, Oct 9, 2026; PriceOfOil wire roundup, Oct 9, 2026; validated crack history refreshed Oct 10, 2026; Reuters, Oct 9, 2026

changes.headline: Saudi airport strikes kill 3; coalition retaliates; US strikes Iran; fresh Hormuz tanker hit
changes.dek: 3 killed at King Khalid Airport (Riyadh); coalition 100+ Houthi targets; Perim Island captured; US struck Iranian targets late Friday; UKMTO tanker hit NW of Oman Saturday 02:00 MDT. Yemen/Saudi (escalating): Thursday - Houthi ballistic missiles hit King Khalid Airport, Riyadh; Saudi aviation authorities confirmed Friday: 3 Saudi nationals killed, several injured, a Saudia pilot killed, an aircraft damaged; airport closed then reopened. Earlier in the week: 3 killed, 36 injured at Abha and King Khalid airports (Wednesday); Jazan and Najran also hit; Saudi Arabia intercepted 3 ballistic missiles including 2 toward Riyadh. Saturday - the coalition says it destroyed 100+ Houthi targets in a large-scale operation. Ground: Yemeni government forces captured Perim Island and recaptured areas around Bab al-Mandeb (Oct 9), reducing Houthi access to shipping lanes. Houthis threaten further strikes on Saudi oil facilities and warned airlines to avoid Saudi airspace. Hormuz/Iran: Thursday - Iran launched 4 one-way attack drones at ships in the Strait (3 intercepted, 1 struck the M/V Ever Lovely); late Friday - the US struck Iranian military targets in retaliation; Saturday ~02:00 MDT - UKMTO reported a tanker struck NW of Oman (bridge damaged, crew safe). Diplomacy contradictory: Trump claims 'constructive talks,' no strike before Nov 3 midterms, 'fully enforced' blockade; Iran's FM says Tehran is reviewing the US response to its 7-day Strait-reopening proposal. US sanctioned 17 vessels Thursday for Iranian crude transport. OPEC+ (Oct 4): November quotas held unchanged at 31.01 Mb/d combined; August actual ~25 Mb/d.
changes.balance_read: Escalation is now two-sided: US retaliation and Houthi threats against Saudi oil facilities vs. a claimed diplomatic track and a 7-day Strait-reopening proposal under review.

changes.headline: SPR exchange award pending; Gulf sour pricing awaits
changes.dek: SPR 40 Mbbl exchange award still pending (deadline corrected to Oct 6, 11:00 CT). The SPR exchange award is still pending - no DOE announcement as of early Saturday. Correction: the bid deadline was 11:00 AM CT Tuesday, October 6 (energy.gov), not Oct 7 as the Oct 9 edition said. Solicitation: up to 40 Mbbl of sour (Big Hill + Bryan Mound), Nov-Dec 2026 delivery, exchange structure; the final US tranche of the 172 Mbbl commitment under the March IEA coordinated release. SPR sits at ~284 Mbbl, the lowest since 1982.
changes.balance_read: The exchange award is the next real data point for Gulf sour pricing; the Merey-vs-WCS-vs-Mars triangle at the Gulf is the comp-barrel trade against WCS length.

changes.headline: Positioning: WTI specs light (29th percentile); Brent still long 201k
changes.dek: WTI MM net +53,598 (29th pct); Brent MM net +201,052; Brent Sep-29 corrected to +204,302. New COT vintage (as-of Tue Oct 6, released Fri Oct 9): NYMEX WTI managed-money net +53,598 (-25,994 w/w) - 29th percentile of the 1-year range, the long book cut 30.7k in a week; the WTI long overhang is largely gone. ICE Brent managed-money net +201,052 (-3,250 w/w) - still a long-heavy book against only ~110k of MM shorts. Correction: the Oct 9 edition carried Brent Sep-29 net as +63,651 (column mis-parse); the true Sep-29 print was +204,302. True Brent series: +265,753 (Sep 8) -> +282,657 (Sep 15) -> +218,114 (Sep 22) -> +204,302 (Sep 29) -> +201,052 (Oct 6). The COT predates the Oct 8-9 price action entirely.
changes.balance_read: Specs went into the Oct 8-9 rally positioned light on WTI - a bearish headline has little left to flush there; an escalation shock meets thin length with room for a catch-up rally. Brent's remaining flush risk is on a de-escalation headline.
